- FLEX-2: Experimental Study of Initial Diameter Effects on Convection-free Droplet Combustion in the Standard Atmosphere for n-Heptane, n-Octane, and n-Decane: International Space Station and Ground-based Experiments; n-Butanol droplet combustion: Numerical modeling and reduced… [S1]
- CFI: Can cool flames support quasi-steady alkane droplet burning?; Cool-flame extinction during n-alkane droplet combustion in microgravity; Partial-Burning Regime for Quasi-Steady Droplet Combustion Supported by Cool Flames; The role of cool-flame chemistry in quasi-steady… [S2]
- FLEX: Methanol Droplet Combustion in Oxygen-Inert Environments in Microgravity; Methanol Droplet Extinction in Oxygen/Carbon-dioxide/Nitrogen Mixtures in Microgravity: Results from the International Space Station Experiments; A Numerical Study On The Extinction Characteristics Of… [S3]
- FLEX: Flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity and effectiveness of gaseous suppressants (CO2, He) — 274 droplet tests with measured burning rate, extinction diameter and end state. [S4]
- ACME BRE: ACME BRE Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator. Flames of Gaseous Fuels. Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME [S5]
- BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2: BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1. Limitation: Outcome annotations  [S10]

- Only documents in this knowledge base were searched.

sources.title: BASS-II — Burning and Suppression of Solids - II — hypothesis
sources.text: flammability of the material on Earth. However, it may not be conservative for flammability in space. Testing at constant O2 mole fractions permits studying flame spread and extinction at low and high flow speed. We are interested in finding the fundamental limit for a given material.

sources.title: BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2
sources.text: BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1. Limitation: Outcome annotations are free text; flow units to be confirmed in the BASS-II documentation; flame-spread rates are in the raw video data.

sources.title: Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K
sources.text: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity. Limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a finding.

sources.title: More oxygen: droplet flames more often survive to burnout
sources.text: FLEX droplet tests in N2-only atmospheres that ended in flame extinction before burnout — Heptane: 5/17 at 21 % O2 vs 0/11 at 30–34 % O2; Methanol: 9/12 at 21 % O2 vs 2/13 at 30–34 % O2. Remaining tests ended in burnout ('completion') or droplet disruption. Limitation: Isolated droplets, two fuels; 'extinction' here means the flame went out before the droplet was consumed (often radiative), not the action of an extinguisher. Counts, not a model.

sources.title: Stopping ventilation may not be enough in oxygen-enriched cabins
sources.text: In quiescent microgravity, BRE flames emulating condensed materials (e.g. PMMA, nylon) kept burning quasi-steadily in the elevated-oxygen atmospheres considered for future spacecraft, whereas comparable flames at 21 % O2 self-extinguished in a short time. PSI describes these results as preliminary. Limitation: Gaseous emulation of solids; per-test pressure not in the summary table; results flagged preliminary.
